keystone_enabler.title: Transport FSoulSiegePreparation through the campaign battle bridge
keystone_enabler.label: DP
keystone_enabler.statement: Add preparation to FSoulCampaignBattleDescriptor and feed FSoulSiegeRules::Begin(Prep) instead of Begin({}).

verified_gap.label: VCS
verified_gap.detail: SoulRealtimeBattleArena.cpp:1264 constructs SiegeState=FSoulSiegeRules::Begin({}) then overrides only GateMaximum/GateIntegrity from Encounter->SiegeGateMaximum/SiegeGateIntegrity (SoulFounderPlaytestStateSubsystem.cpp:954-955). bLadders/bBatteringRam/bSiegeTower/bWallBreach/bReinforcedGate/bAmmoStores/bMagicalWard are all left default. The descriptor (SoulCampaignBattleBridge.h) carries bSiege + gate ints but NO preparation.

keystone_enabler.why_keystone: Every engine and the ladder vector are gated on their preparation boolean being populated. Without B1, each engine would need its own ad-hoc transport (a second authority). B1 is the single clean seam.
acceptance: Descriptor serializes preparation; result/save unaffected (reuse existing Soul.Settlements + campaign domains).
Round-trips through F5/F9 like the existing optional siege-result summary fields (SoulFounderPlaytestStateSubsystem.cpp:711-714,880).
Default (no prep) reproduces exact V0 behavior — regression-locked.

engines.name: Battering ram
engines.label: DP
engines.rationale_vcs: Reuses the existing, qualified gate-damage path FSoulSiegeRules::ApplyGateDamage + CommitSiegeHit/CommitGateMelee. A ram is conceptually a high-damage, multi-crew melee contact on the SAME portcullis target V0 already damages. CanAssaultWalls already returns true for bBatteringRam.
design: Deployable ASoulSiegeRamActor crewed by N attackers; produces large accepted AcceptedDamage per contact vs the gate (bounded, finite, replay-protected via AcceptedContacts like V0).
Ram advances the SAME GateIntegrityPermille; at zero reuses OpenSiegeGate.
Ram is destructible/haltable by defenders (fire/ranged) so it is not a guaranteed win.

assets.label: LRC
assets.note: No catalogued product is named 'battering ram'. A ram mesh may be sourceable from an owned medieval/castle kit (Ravenhold / Modular Castle / Fantasy Medieval Castle Kit, all VOA owned) OR authored simply. Mesh source is LRC; the RULE does not depend on a specific mesh.

unknowns: Ram crew pathing to the measured gate base in the authored map (LRC).

engines.name: Catapult / Mangonel (recommend ONE engine of this class)
engines.preparation_flag: none existing; needs a new bounded prep field OR reuse bWallBreach as 'ranged breach capability'
engines.label: DP
engines.rationale: Delivers ranged gate/wall damage from the outer field, producing breaches (feeds wall-breach vector B2 and defender depth D). Introduces a projectile arc + wall-SEGMENT damage model that does not exist for walls today (gate damage exists; segment damage in-battle does not).

owned_asset.label: VOA
owned_asset.recommendation: Use the OWNED mangonel as the single engine of this class. Do NOT also plan trebuchet + ballista + catapult; one ranged engine keeps the new projectile/segment-damage model to one qualification pass.

related_owned_assets.label: VOA
related_owned_assets.note: Alternative/secondary ranged engine; defer. Keep ONE ranged engine for V1.

existing_projectile_hooks.label: VCS
existing_projectile_hooks.detail: A projectile/ranged path exists for archers: URBCombatRangedComponent + PresentBowLaunch + FRBProjectileLaunch + ASoulBattleSpellProjectile (SoulRealtimeBattleArena.h/.cpp). A mangonel projectile could extend this rather than invent a new projectile authority.

design: Static-ish engine at an outer-field emplacement; fires an arcing projectile at the gate or a wall segment.
Gate hit reuses ApplyGateDamage; wall-segment hit needs a NEW in-battle wall-segment integrity model (see ENGINE-WALLSEG).
Bounded rate of fire + finite ammo (tie to bAmmoStores semantics or a prep count).
unknowns: Is the mangonel locally downloaded/importable? (VOA: owned, not local, not imported.)
Projectile arc tuning against the authored map scale (LRC).

engines.name: In-battle wall-segment damage model (shared dependency for catapult + wall breach)
engines.label: DP
engines.rationale_vcs: ASoulFortificationSegmentActor already models Intact/Damaged/Breached/Repair visual branches (SoulFortificationSegmentActor.cpp) and FSoulSettlementState has WallIntegrityPermille + DamageWalls/RepairWalls (SoulSettlement.cpp). BUT in-battle wall damage currently ONLY exists for the gate; the segment actor's breach visual is driven ONLY by the TOWN-VIEW presentation controller (SoulSettlementPresentationController.cpp:109-123), always with bRepairing=false. There is no in-battle wall-segment integrity.
design: Add a per-segment integrity to FSoulSiegeState (NOT a new authority): extend WallBreaches/OpenBreach to track which segment breached.
A segment reaching zero opens a physical passage (feature B2) and advances ESoulSiegeLayer::Walls.
On resolve, feed the breach to FSoulSiegeAftermath.ScarIds so the breach persists in the town view (existing path).
unknowns: Which authored wall actors in L_HumanCapital_Authored can carry a breach state + nav behind them (LRC).

engines.name: Siege tower
engines.label: DP
engines.rationale: A mobile high platform that delivers a column of troops onto the wall-top. It is the single most demanding item: it needs mobile collision, a deploy/dock animation, a bridge-drop, AND the same authored wall-top standable nav that ladders need. CanAssaultWalls already honors bSiegeTower.
design: Deployable ASoulSiegeTowerActor that pathes to a wall face (reusing the measured-approach discipline of SiegeDeployment/route survey).
On dock, drops a ramp to the wall-top landing (same landing requirement as LADDER-R3).
Troops traverse the ramp onto the wall-top; defenders contest (Phase D).

assets.label: LRC
assets.note: No catalogued 'siege tower' product. Tower mesh likely authored or kitbashed from owned castle kits (VOA). Mesh is not functionality.

unknowns: Mobile-object pathing + collision across the authored approach (the V0 route survey already found an authored bridge deck gap near the gate — SiegeDeployment comment — a wide tower could re-trigger that; LRC).

reinforced_gate_and_support.label: VCS
reinforced_gate_and_support.detail: DEFENDER-side preparation already works end to end: bReinforcedGate -> GateMaximum 1300 (SoulSiege.cpp Begin) and the campaign already sets SiegeGateMaximum=1300 at FortificationLevel>=2 (SoulFounderPlaytestStateSubsystem.cpp:954). bAmmoStores/bMagicalWard set bArmoryActive/bMagicWardActive in Begin but have no runtime consumer yet.
reinforced_gate_and_support.proposal: V1 should give bAmmoStores (defender ranged resupply) and bMagicalWard (reduce incoming engine/magic effect) real runtime effect, so defender preparation is symmetric with attacker engines.

local_validation_ids.ENGINE-NAV-1: Engine/crew pathing to its emplacement or wall face in L_HumanCapital_Authored, including the known authored bridge-deck gap near the gate.
local_validation_ids.ENGINE-COL-1: Engine collision solid; mobile engines do not clip walls; wall-segment breach collision opens a real passage.
local_validation_ids.ENGINE-ANIM-1: Operate/fire/dock animations present and retargeted; rule-only fallback if not.
local_validation_ids.ENGINE-VFX-1: Projectile/impact VFX present; rule correctness independent of VFX.

feasibility_ranking_summary: 1. Battering ram (ENGINE-RAM): reuses qualified gate-damage path. SHIP FIRST among engines.
2. Catapult/Mangonel (ENGINE-CATAPULT) + wall-segment model (ENGINE-WALLSEG): owned asset, new projectile+segment risk, ONE engine of this class only.
3. Siege tower (ENGINE-TOWER): highest nav/collision/animation risk, depends on real wall-top. QUALIFY LAST.
explicit_unknowns: FSoulSiegePreparation is never transported today; B1 is unbuilt (VCS). All engine prep flags are latent.
No in-battle wall-segment damage exists; only the gate takes battle damage (VCS).
Mangonel + ballista are owned but not locally present/imported (VOA).
Authored map wall-top + breachable segments + mobile-engine pathing are all unproven (LRC).
